bias: Rate-of-change framing: financial conditions have eased meaningfully over the past three weeks (TGA draining, reserves rebuilding, dollar and USDJPY softening, VIX crushed today) even though absolute yield levels remain restrictive and the RRP buffer is nearly exhausted. Oil's 12% run since the last snapshot is the one clear inflation-side threat to the disinflation thesis.

supporting: TGA draining, reserves rebuilding — net liquidity +$104B since last check
DXY and USDKRW both weaker — dollar pressure easing
against: Oil +12.2% since last check — disinflation thesis under pressure
HY OAS widened 20bps, CACC down double digits
Nominal yields rising across the curve (10Y +10bp, 30Y +15bp)
RRP buffer nearly empty at $1.08B — little liquidity cushion left
KOSPI still -22.8% and SOXX -10.1% versus last snapshot despite today's bounce
counterargs.read: Today reads as a sharp relief rally after a real multi-week drawdown (KOSPI -22.8%, SOXX -10.1%, EWY -10.7% net of today's bounce). Plumbing has genuinely improved — TGA draining, reserves rising, dollar softer — which supports the bounce. But rising nominal yields alongside a 12% oil rally keep the inflation/duration risk alive, and a nearly-empty RRP buffer means there's little dry powder left if funding stress reappears. Treat this as a tactical bounce inside a still-fragile structural backdrop, not a confirmed regime shift.

trade_table.rationale: SOXX +8.5%, DRAM +16.7% today; ratio to SPY still depressed vs 3wk ago (0.68 vs 0.75).
EWY +11.8% today but still below SMA20 (161.21 vs 170.29); KOSPI far below 8,200 gate level despite USDKRW passing.
10Y/30Y yields rising since last check; TLT -1.8%; oil-driven inflation risk keeps duration unattractive near-term.
CACC -10.5%, COF +7.0% — dispersion suggests idiosyncratic, not systemic, credit stress.

duration_score.reason: 10Y and 30Y yields are rising (not falling) alongside stable-to-softer breakevens, while risk assets rally hard — a 'good news is good news' pattern rather than the classic James pain trade. Real 5Y (DFII5) sits at 2.19%; nominal front-end (US02Y) ticked up modestly. This isn't the sharp real-rate-tightening pain trade seen in the prior snapshot, but rising nominal yields into an oil rally is a mild headwind for duration.
